children: Our Bureau New Delhi: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman will meet CEOs of the Government of Singapore Investment Corporation, Temasek Holdings, DBS Bank Ltd, Standard Chartered Bank, British International Investment and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, among others, during her three-day visit to Singapore from October 9 to 11, the government said Friday.

Singapore is India's largest source of foreign direct investment (FDI), with cumulative inflows of around $194.68 billion between April 2000 and March 2026. "Singaporean institutional investors, including GIC and Temasek, have significant investments across the Indian economy," the finance ministry said in a statement.

As part of her engagements with the investment community, Sitharaman will meet leading Singaporean and international investors, financial institutions and business leaders at a roundtable with hedge fund and portfolio fund managers, as well as through a series of government-to-business meetings. "The interaction will provide an opportunity for an exchange of views with leading global investors on India's growth trajectory, investment opportunities and the evolving global economic and financial landscape," the ministry said. It added that platforms such as the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund and GIFT City could provide avenues for greater participation by Singaporean capital, including through investment vehicles and funds.

During the visit, Sitharaman will call on Singapore President Tharman Shanmugaratnam, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, deputy prime minister Gan Kim Yong and foreign minister Vivian Balakrishnan. "The discussions will cover key areas of the India-Singapore Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and take forward the outcomes of the ISMR, including cooperation in trade and investment, digital financial connectivity, capital markets, taxation, semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, skilling and aviation," the ministry said.

The visit underscores India's commitment to deepening its comprehensive strategic partnership with Singapore, with a focus on leveraging strong political ties to promote investment, business partnerships and concrete economic outcomes, it said. title: FM in Singapore to Tap Investors, Funds
